body:
We make Kiron, and Kiron imports some of these files, so weigh this accordingly. Each app's steps come from its own help pages and App Store listing, checked November 15, 2026; where an app doesn't publish a step, we say so and name our source. Everything about Kiron describes version 1.2.

Your workout log is years of effort you can't recreate. Exporting it gives you a copy to keep when you switch apps, cancel a subscription, or just want to look at your numbers. Every app puts the button somewhere different, and two of the six here don't put it in the app at all.

Most give you a CSV file: a plain table that Google Sheets, Excel or Numbers can open, usually with one row for each set you logged. Here's where each app keeps its export, what's in the file, and where it can go next.

Where each app's export lives, as of November 15, 2026
AppWhere to find itWhat you getWatch out for
FitbodIn the app: Settings, Export Workout DataA CSV file, one row per setCheck the unit in the weight column's name
StrongIn the app: Settings, Export Strong Data (Export Data on Android)A CSV file, one row per setThe file often doesn't say pounds or kilograms
HevyIn the app: Profile, Settings, Export & Import Data, Export Data, Export WorkoutsA CSV file, one row per setBody measurements are a separate export
JEFITOn jefit.com: Settings, Data Controls, Export DataOne file with your whole historyNot in the app; the file comes in sections
BoostcampNo export documentedNo fileAsk support for a copy
StrongLiftsIn the app: Settings, Export DataA CSV file, by emailA second route if the paywall blocks you

Three habits that save trouble

  • Export before you cancel or delete your account. JEFIT's FAQ, for one, warns that deleting your account removes your history for good.
  • Switch the app to English first if you'll import the file somewhere else. Column names follow the app's language, and importers look for the English ones: Hevy's help center asks for Strong files exported in English, and Kiron reads English exports only.
  • Keep the original file. Save it somewhere safe and work on a copy. Re-saving a CSV in a spreadsheet can change how dates are written, and it can break JEFIT's file.

Fitbod

  1. Open Fitbod's Settings. Independent guides put it behind the gear icon on the Log tab.
  2. Tap Export Workout Data.
  3. Save the file to Files, or email it to yourself.

What's in it: one row per set, with the date and time, exercise, reps, weight, time, distance, whether the set was a warm-up, and a note. The weight column's name includes its unit, such as Weight(kg). Guides disagree on whether that follows your Fitbod setting, so check it against a lift you know.

Fitbod's help center doesn't document its export (we searched it on November 15, 2026). These are the steps Kiron's import screen gives, and two independent guides describe the same path.

Strong

  1. Open Strong's Settings.
  2. Tap Export Strong Data. Strong's help center says the Android app calls it Export Data.
  3. Save or share the file. Strong's App Store listing says it goes to Notes or email.

What's in it: one row per set, with the date, workout name, exercise, weight, reps, distance, time, notes and an effort rating. The weight column usually doesn't say pounds or kilograms, so check a lift you know. Strong's help center says Strong can't import the file back, so keep it.

Hevy

  1. Open your Profile, then Settings (the gear icon).
  2. Tap Export & Import Data, then Export Data.
  3. Choose Export Workouts. Export Measurements gives you a separate file of body measurements.

What's in it: one row per set, with the workout's title and times, exercise, superset, notes, set type, weight, reps, distance, time and effort rating. The unit is in the column name, such as weight_kg or weight_lbs, so there's nothing to guess.

JEFIT

JEFIT's export is on its website, not in the app, and its FAQ says every account can use it, paid or not:

  1. Log in at jefit.com.
  2. Open Settings.
  3. Go to Data Controls and choose Export Data.

What's in it: JEFIT's FAQ doesn't say. Apps that import JEFIT files describe one CSV file covering your whole history, split into several sections and named after your username and the date. Open a copy, not the original.

Boostcamp

Boostcamp doesn't document a way to export your history: there's nothing in its FAQ, its App Store description or its recent release notes, checked November 15, 2026. Your options:

  • Ask support for a copy. Boostcamp's privacy policy (last updated November 27, 2024) says people in the EU, UK and EEA have a right to a copy of their data they can take elsewhere, as may people in California and some other US states. Requests go through its contact page, and asking costs nothing wherever you live.
  • Copy it by hand. For a short history, typing your main lifts into a spreadsheet is slow but reliable.
  • Be careful with browser extensions. Some say they can save your history from Boostcamp's website. They aren't made by Boostcamp, we haven't checked them, and they'd need access to your account.

StrongLifts

StrongLifts' support page, updated October 17, 2026, gives two routes. The usual one:

  1. Open StrongLifts and go to Settings, then Export Data.
  2. Your data appears as a CSV document.
  3. Tap the Share button to email yourself a copy.

If the paywall is in the way: StrongLifts has been subscription-only since 2025, and 4 of its 500 most recent US App Store reviews said that kept them from their old data. The support page now covers that case: tap the menu icon in the top right corner, tap Contact Support, and send the pre-filled email to your own address. Your data arrives in that email as a CSV document. StrongLifts doesn't list the file's columns, so open it in a spreadsheet to see what came across.

Where each file can go

What can read each export, as of November 15, 2026
Export fromHevyKironA spreadsheet
FitbodNo official importYesYes
StrongYesYesYes
HevyNo: Hevy imports Strong files onlyYesYes
JEFITNo official importNoYes, with some tidying
StrongLiftsNo official importNoYes

Boostcamp isn't listed because there's no documented file to move. Other apps advertise importers for some of these files too, so check the help pages of the app you're moving to.

Into Hevy: Strong files

In Hevy, go to Profile, Settings, Export & Import Data, Import Data, Import Strong CSV, then choose the file. Hevy's help center asks for an unedited Strong export, in English and in kilograms. It takes one file at a time, and you can remove an import from the same screen. Your finished workouts come across; routines don't, and supersets arrive as separate exercises. For other apps' history, Hevy's support team can send a sample file in Strong's format for you to fill in.

Into Kiron: Fitbod, Strong and Hevy files

In Kiron, open Settings, tap Import from another app, then Choose file. New users also see it during setup, as "Bring your workout history". Nothing is saved until you've checked a preview:

  • What's in the file: how many workouts, their dates, and how many working sets, not counting warm-ups. Workouts already in Kiron are skipped, so importing a file twice doesn't double anything.
  • Pounds or kilograms: when a file doesn't say, as Strong's often doesn't, Kiron shows your heaviest set and asks. It asks about miles or kilometers the same way.
  • How your exercises matched: each is matched to Kiron's exercise library, with doubtful ones under "Worth a check". Tap any one to use the suggested match, pick another exercise, or keep it as your own.

Kiron brings in finished workouts only, so routines and programs stay behind, and it needs a connection while it works. You can remove an import later from the same screen; workouts you logged in Kiron stay.

Once your history is in, Kiron uses it to set your weights: lifts you've done before start from your last numbers, a little lighter if it's been more than four weeks.

Kiron has no export of its own in version 1.2, so keep your original file.

Into a spreadsheet: everything

Every file here opens in Google Sheets, Excel or Numbers. Two tips:

  • Use the spreadsheet's import option rather than double-clicking the file, so dates aren't changed. If everything lands in one column, choose semicolon as the separator: some apps use semicolons in countries where the comma is the decimal point.
  • Filter by exercise. With one row per set, as in the Fitbod, Strong and Hevy files, filtering the exercise column shows a lift's whole history, ready to chart. Split JEFIT's sections onto separate sheets first.

Tempted to train from the spreadsheet itself? Our comparison of workout spreadsheets and apps covers the trade-offs.

If you're switching apps

Exporting is the easy half; choosing where to go is the harder one. We've written that up app by app, and each post says who should stay put: alternatives to Strong, alternatives to Fitbod, what to do now StrongLifts is subscription-only and Hevy vs Kiron. For the wider view, workout apps for following a program sorts eight apps by who writes the plan.

And the pitch, once. Kiron (that's us) is a workout app for {{kiron:cell-platforms}} that runs your training plan: one of {{kiron:program-count}} ready-made programs, one built from a few answers, or the plan you already have, pasted in or photographed, with runs on the same calendar as your lifting. Bring your Fitbod, Strong or Hevy history, and your first weights come from it. {{kiron:offline-lead}} {{kiron:offline-detail}} {{kiron:pricing-sentence}} If all you want is a safe home for your history, a spreadsheet does that for free. See what Kiron does.

Common questions

Can you export your data from Fitbod?

Yes. In Fitbod's Settings, tap Export Workout Data and save the CSV file. It has one row per set, and the weight column's name includes its unit.

How do I move my Strong workouts to Hevy?

Export from Strong (Settings, Export Strong Data) with the app set to English. Then in Hevy, go to Profile, Settings, Export & Import Data, Import Data, Import Strong CSV, and choose the file. Your finished workouts come across; your routines don't.

Can I export my workout history from Boostcamp?

Not with a documented button, as of November 15, 2026. Ask Boostcamp's support team for a copy through its contact page.

Do I need JEFIT Elite to export my logs?

No. JEFIT's FAQ says every account can export, on jefit.com: Settings, Data Controls, Export Data.

Can I get my StrongLifts data out without subscribing?

Yes. StrongLifts' support page gives a route for anyone stuck on the paywall: tap the menu icon in the top right corner, then Contact Support, and send the pre-filled email to yourself. Your data comes back as a CSV document.
